title: 5 Best ChatGPT Prompts for Debugging Code (2026)
description: A five-step debugging sequence that takes you from raw error to verified fix — reproduce, isolate, explain, fix, and prevent — instead of pasting an error and hoping.

steps.title: Explain the error properly
steps.promptText:
You are a senior [LANGUAGE] engineer. I'm hitting this error:

[PASTE FULL ERROR + STACK TRACE]

Relevant code:
[PASTE THE 20-40 LINES AROUND THE FAILURE]

Explain: (1) what this error literally means, (2) the 3 most likely causes ranked by probability IN THIS CODE, (3) what evidence in the stack trace points to each. Do not suggest fixes yet.
steps.whyThisTool: ChatGPT is strongest at fast, broad error-pattern recognition across languages.
steps.outputExpected: A ranked list of likely causes tied to specific lines in your stack trace — not generic advice.

steps.title: Build a minimal reproduction
steps.promptText: Based on cause #[N] from your last answer, write the smallest possible standalone script that should reproduce this error. Use no external dependencies beyond [LIST DEPS]. If the repro needs specific data, generate realistic fake data inline.
steps.whyThisTool: A minimal repro turns guessing into testing — ChatGPT scaffolds these quickly.
steps.outputExpected: A runnable snippet under ~30 lines that either reproduces the bug (cause confirmed) or doesn't (cause eliminated).

steps.title: Trace the actual values
steps.promptText:
Here's what happened when I ran the repro: [PASTE OUTPUT].

Walk through the code line by line as an interpreter would, tracking the value of [VARIABLE(S)] at each step. Show a table: line number | variable | value | note. Flag the exact line where reality diverges from intent.
steps.whyThisTool: Forcing a line-by-line trace catches the off-by-one assumptions everyone skims past.
steps.outputExpected: A value-trace table with one clearly flagged divergence point.

steps.title: Fix with constraints
steps.promptText: Now fix it. Constraints: keep the public API unchanged, don't add dependencies, match the existing code style, and explain WHY the fix works in 2 sentences. Then list any edge cases the fix might still miss.
steps.whyThisTool: Constrained fixes prevent the classic AI rewrite-everything failure mode.
steps.outputExpected: A minimal diff-style fix plus an honest edge-case list.

steps.title: Prevent the recurrence
steps.promptText: Write a regression test that would have caught this bug, in [TEST FRAMEWORK]. Then suggest one lint rule, type annotation, or assertion that would make this whole class of bug impossible in this codebase.
steps.whyThisTool: Turning a fix into a test + guardrail is what separates debugging from firefighting.
steps.outputExpected: One failing-before/passing-after test and one structural prevention suggestion.

faq.q: Do these prompts work with Claude or Gemini too?
faq.a: Yes — the sequence is tool-agnostic. We verify it against ChatGPT because its error-pattern coverage is the broadest, but you can run every step in Claude or Gemini unchanged.

faq.q: Why five steps instead of just asking for a fix?
faq.a: Pasting an error and asking for a fix works for trivial bugs. This sequence exists for the other kind: it confirms the cause before fixing, so you don't apply a confident-sounding wrong patch.

faq.q: What should I replace the [PLACEHOLDERS] with?
faq.a: Anything in brackets is yours to fill: language, stack trace, code, framework. The prompts are designed so each placeholder is obvious in context.

benefit: Fix the bug on the first try — confirm the cause before you patch it.
